/-!
# Mathoverflow 31809

Source:
[Mathoverflow/31809](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/31809/pre-triangulated-category-that-isnt-triangulated)

namespace Mathoverflow31809

open CategoryTheory Limits Category Preadditive Pretriangulated

/-- Does there exist a category that is pretriangulated but not triangulated? -/
@[category research open, AMS 18]
theorem mathoverflow_31809 : answer(sorry) ↔ (∀ (C : Type*) [Category C] [Preadditive C]
    [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C], IsTriangulated C) := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow31809

findings.description: The unnegated universal statement on lines 33–35 reverses the source's existence question. Let E mean that some pretriangulated category, with its specified distinguished triangles, is not triangulated. The Lean right-hand side says that every such structure is triangulated, which is equivalent to ¬E, not E. Consequently, answer(True) would mean that no requested example exists, rather than that one exists. In the scratch file I proved the right-hand side ↔ ¬E and that the two formulations cannot use the same answer. This polarity defect is independent of the problem's subsequent resolution.
findings.source_evidence: The cited MathOverflow question begins by discussing the lack of a known 'pre-triangulated category that is not triangulated'; part 2 asks 'what is an example of a pre-triangulated category that is not a triangulated category?' https://mathoverflow.net/questions/31809/pre-triangulated-category-that-isnt-triangulated
findings.suggested_fix: Negate the existing universal right-hand side: `answer(sorry) ↔ ¬ (∀ (C : Type*) [Category C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C], IsTriangulated C)`. Equivalently, existentially quantify the category and all its structures and conclude `¬ IsTriangulated C`. Apply the separate status/answer update described below.

status_issues.source_status: The MathOverflow answer dated 11 August 2026 reports a counterexample by Xiao-Wu Chen, Jian Liu, Xue-Song Lu, and Chencheng Zhang, arXiv:2608.09777, submitted 10 August 2026. Its main theorem constructs a pretriangulated structure on finitely generated projective modules over the type-A₅ preprojective algebra over 𝔽₂ that fails TR4. The source therefore now records a positive answer to the existence question, or a negative answer to the file's universal predicate.
status_issues.evidence: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/31809/pre-triangulated-category-that-isnt-triangulated#514138 says the linked paper 'constructs a pre-triangulated category which is not triangulated'. Theorem 1.2 (`thm:main`) and the abstract of https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09777 state this construction. The earlier contrary claim in arXiv:1506.00887 was withdrawn and is not the basis for this update.
status_issues.suggested_change: Update to `@[category research solved]` and cite arXiv:2608.09777. For the source-aligned existence predicate (or negated universal predicate), use `answer(True)`. The existing unnegated universal predicate would instead require `answer(False)`.

reformulations.difference: The hypothesis package does not explicitly require finite biproducts, although the source's standard definition begins with an additive category. This is a faithful modelling choice, separate from the answer-polarity defect.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib derives `HasFiniteBiproducts C` from the stated preadditive, zero-object, shift, and pretriangulated hypotheses via `Pretriangulated.instHasFiniteBiproducts`. Thus explicitly adding finite biproducts does not change the range of eligible structured categories. I proved a ↔ between the current universal predicate and the same predicate with an additional `HasFiniteBiproducts C` hypothesis; I also checked the analogous existential equivalence.

Historical calibration: /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr00054.md, pr00055.md, pr01163.md, pr01191.md, pr04019.md, pr04119.md
review.notes: The sole declaration and the semantics of all its hypotheses and conclusion were checked. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully. Tests establish the polarity reversal without using the imported sorry theorem, verify the redundant finite-biproduct hypothesis, exclude empty categories through HasZeroObject, and construct an explicit one-object zero category satisfying all the hypotheses and IsTriangulated. No additional mathematical defects were found.

submission.summary: Negated the universal predicate so the statement asks for a pretriangulated category that is not triangulated. Updated the status to research solved, recorded answer(True), and added the verified 2026 counterexample reference. The file compiles with only the permitted declaration-uses-sorry warning.

/-!

[CLLZ26] Chen, X.-W., Liu, J., Lu, X.-S., and Zhang, C.,

namespace Mathoverflow31809

open CategoryTheory Limits Category Preadditive Pretriangulated

/--
Does there exist a category that is pretriangulated but not triangulated?

Answered affirmatively by Chen, Liu, Lu, and Zhang [CLLZ26, Theorem 1.2].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 18]
theorem mathoverflow_31809 : answer(True) ↔ ¬ (∀ (C : Type*) [Category C] [Preadditive C]
    [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C], IsTriangulated C) := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow31809
